answer: Interleaved Arrival Mirror. Each identity must submit its first N messages as a fixed-shape burst; a relay delays and reshapes all traffic so every sender's arrival pattern is a mirror of a random reference schedule, checked against an onyx-tagged audit log. Any deviation flags the signal as synthetic and throttles it. An attacker must spin up and pace each fake identity's burst independently, paying real wall-clock time and per-identity relay bandwidth to mimic genuine arrival cadence.
